proposals.before: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year, Li Hongzhang and Liu Kunyi relayed Nie Jigui's report that British and American post offices in Shanghai planned new branch offices at every port—making any later Chinese expansion far harder.
proposals.after: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year, Li Hongzhang and Liu Kunyi relayed Nie Jigui's report that the British and American municipal councils in Shanghai were now planning to add letter offices at the various ports—making any later Chinese expansion far harder.
proposals.reason: Chinese 英、美工部局 denotes the British and American municipal councils (Works Bureaus), not post offices; 信局 are the letter offices they planned to add.

proposals.before: Since the eighteenth year, a single U.S. postal revenue statement listed collections of sixty-four trillion, two hundred nine thousand, four hundred ninety dollars.
proposals.after: Since the eighteenth year, a single U.S. postal revenue statement listed collections of sixty-four million two hundred nine thousand four hundred ninety dollars.
proposals.reason: In this fiscal context 六十四兆二十萬九千四百九十 means 64,209,490; rendering 兆 as trillion yields an impossible figure.

proposals.before: Tracing back from the eighteenth year, on a single postal statement sheet for the United States alone, the silver dollars collected reached as many as sixty-four trillion, two hundred nine thousand, four hundred ninety dollars.
proposals.after: Tracing back from the eighteenth year, on a single postal statement sheet for the United States alone, the silver dollars collected reached as many as sixty-four million two hundred nine thousand four hundred ninety dollars.
proposals.reason: Same 兆-to-million correction as in the idiomatic field for the U.S. postal revenue figure.

proposals.before: Its mail, ordinary and special, totaled three hundred million plus sixty-two million two hundred ten thousand six hundred thirty-nine pieces.
proposals.after: Its mail, ordinary and special, totaled three hundred million plus sixty-two million two hundred twenty-one thousand six hundred thirty-nine pieces.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六千二百二十一萬 has 二百二十一 (221), not two hundred ten.

decisions.reason: s0043 has 上海英、美工部局現議增設各口信局: 工部局 are the British and American municipal councils, and 信局 are the letter offices they planned to add. The prior idiomatic wrongly turns 工部局 into post offices and 信局 into branch offices; the proposed wording restores both terms.

decisions.reason: In s0052, 六十四兆二十萬九千四百九十 in this late-Qing fiscal comparison means 64,209,490 (兆 as million), not sixty-four trillion. The following British figure of 三四千萬 taels confirms the million scale; the proposed idiomatic figure matches the Chinese.

decisions.reason: The same numeral 六十四兆二十萬九千四百九十 must be read as 64,209,490 dollars. The prior literal's trillion reading is impossible beside the British 三四千萬 comparison; the proposed million reading is correct.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六十四兆二十萬九千四百九十圓

decisions.reason: 三萬萬六千二百二十一萬六千二百三十九 is 300,000,000 + 6,221×10,000 + 6,239 = 362,216,239. Expanding 六千二百二十一萬 as sixty-two million two hundred ten thousand is correct; changing it to two hundred twenty-one thousand invents 62,221,000 and conflicts with the idiomatic 362,216,239.
